title: Muse Code: Meta's New Terminal Coding Agent, Explained

facts.fact: Meta released Muse Code, its first terminal-based coding agent, in beta on August 5, 2026, for macOS or Linux.
facts.quote: Muse Code is Meta's first terminal-based coding agent, released in beta on _August 5, 2026_.

facts.fact: Muse Code is powered by Muse Spark 1.2, a coding-focused update to Meta's Muse Spark model family.
facts.quote: It's powered by **Muse Spark 1.2**, a coding-focused update to Meta's Muse Spark model family

facts.fact: Meta's Standard tier for Muse Code charges $1.25 per 1M input tokens, and Meta states it does not train on users' prompts or completions under this tier.
facts.quote: | **Standard** | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 | Meta does **not** train on your prompts or completions |

facts.fact: Meta's Contributor tier for Muse Code charges $0.10 per 1M input tokens, and Meta trains its models on prompts and completions under this tier.
facts.quote: | **Contributor** | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 | Meta **trains its models** on your prompts and completions; capped at 60 requests per minute |

facts.fact: The Muse Code Contributor tier is capped at 60 requests per minute.
facts.quote: Meta **trains its models** on your prompts and completions; capped at 60 requests per minute

facts.fact: The article states the Contributor tier is roughly 12.5x cheaper than Standard on input and 21x cheaper on output for the same model.
facts.quote: The Contributor tier is roughly 12.5x cheaper on input and 21x cheaper on output than Standard — for the identical model.

facts.fact: Meta reports that Muse Spark 1.2 scores 82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 on its own evaluation harness.
facts.quote: Meta reports Muse Spark 1.2 scoring **82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1** and **59.3% on DeepSWE 1.1**

facts.fact: Meta reported a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 80.0 for its predecessor Muse Spark 1.1.
facts.quote: On the **predecessor model, Muse Spark 1.1**, Meta reported a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 80.0.

facts.fact: Vals AI's independent testing measured Muse Spark 1.1 at 69.29 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (third-party).
facts.quote: Vals AI's independent testing measured 69.29 — a gap of more than 10 points.

facts.fact: The Terminal-Bench team's official verified leaderboard lists Muse Spark 1.1 at 76.2% (third-party).
facts.quote: the Terminal-Bench team's own official verified leaderboard entry for Muse Spark 1.1 came in at 76.2%

facts.fact: Artificial Analysis independently puts Muse Spark 1.2 at around 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (third-party), versus Meta's claimed 82.9%.
facts.quote: independent evaluation from Artificial Analysis puts it around 80% against Meta's claimed 82.9%

facts.fact: Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard ranks Muse Spark 1.2 14th (third-party), while Meta's chart places it 2nd.
facts.quote: Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard, by contrast, ranks it **14th**.

facts.fact: The highest independently verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 score reported is 83.8% for Claude Fable 5 running in Claude Code (third-party).
facts.quote: the highest independently verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 score posted by any model so far belongs to Claude Fable 5 running in Claude Code, at 83.8%

facts.fact: Muse Code supports macOS and Linux only at launch, with no confirmed Windows timeline.
facts.quote: Muse Code supports macOS and Linux only at launch, with no confirmed Windows timeline

facts.fact: Muse Code is not open source: its model weights are not released, and access runs through Meta's hosted API and Muse Code itself.
facts.quote: Not open source — weights aren't released, and access runs entirely through Meta's hosted API and Muse Code itself

facts.fact: Muse Code has two paid tiers, Standard and Contributor.
facts.quote: It has two paid tiers: Standard at $1.25/$4.25 per million input/output tokens with no data training, and Contributor at $0.10/$0.20 per million tokens

facts.fact: The Muse Code Standard tier costs $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens, with no training on user data.
facts.quote: Standard at $1.25/$4.25 per million input/output tokens with no data training

facts.fact: The Muse Code Contributor tier costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.20 per million output tokens, and Meta trains on users' prompts and completions in exchange.
facts.quote: Contributor at $0.10/$0.20 per million tokens where Meta trains on your prompts and completions.

facts.fact: The page states the Contributor tier is roughly 12.5x cheaper than Standard on input and 21x cheaper on output.
facts.quote: roughly 12.5x cheaper on input and 21x cheaper on output than Standard

facts.fact: The Muse Code Contributor tier is capped at 60 requests per minute.
facts.quote: It's capped at 60 requests per minute.

facts.fact: Meta says the Muse Code Standard tier does not train on user data.
facts.quote: Use the Standard tier, which Meta says does not train on your data.

facts.fact: The page recommends reserving the Muse Code Contributor tier for open-source, personal, or explicitly non-sensitive work, not client code, NDAs, or regulated data.
facts.quote: The Contributor tier should be reserved for open-source, personal, or explicitly non-sensitive work only

facts.fact: Muse Code does not run on Windows at launch; it supports only macOS and Linux, installed via a single terminal command.
facts.quote: Not at launch. It currently supports macOS and Linux only, installed via a single terminal command.

facts.fact: Meta's own benchmarks place Muse Spark 1.2 close behind Claude Opus 5 (vendor claim).
facts.quote: Meta's own benchmarks place Muse Spark 1.2 close behind Claude Opus 5

facts.fact: Per the page, independent verification, including Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard, ranks Muse Spark 1.2 lower than Meta's launch materials suggest (third-party claim).
facts.quote: independent verification (including Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard) ranks it lower than Meta's launch materials suggest
